column1: # if-filter-rulings.tsv — the FROZEN if:-as-event-filter boundary for ADR-0007
# agent-ingress jobs (issue #1724 AC #2, #6). Each data row rules ONE if: construct
# ALLOW (a pure event predicate the ingress may use) or FORBID (a reach for repo
# state that belongs in the reusable, never the thin caller's if:).
# This file is the MACHINE-READABLE source of the rulings. Story #1725's two guards
# (the ingress if:-linter and its test) consume THESE ROWS DIRECTLY, not the prose
# in the ADR, so the two guards cannot drift apart or disagree on an ambiguous case.
# FORMAT: 4 tab-separated columns, one construct per data row —
#   1 name        stable fixture key the guards look up by
#   2 verdict     ALLOW | FORBID
#   3 expression  a representative if:-expression fragment exercising the construct
#   4 rationale   why the verdict holds (the boundary principle, not a repo detail)
# PRINCIPLE: an if: is evaluated by the Actions service BEFORE a runner exists, so
# it can only ever see the delivered event. github.event_name, github.event.action
# and payload fields read as a plain predicate are the delta that woke the ingress
# — ALLOW. Anything that reaches org/repo configuration, another job's computed
# output, the repo tree, repo identity, or a human-mutated repo-state snapshot
# riding in the payload is repo state, not the event — FORBID; it belongs in the
# reusable as an explicit, permissioned step.
# name
vars
column4: Org/repo configuration variables are repo state, not event data — set out of band, unrelated to the delivered event.

column1: secrets
column4: Secrets are repo/org configuration, never part of the event payload; probing them in an if: is a repo-state reach.

column1: needs-outputs
column4: needs.*.outputs.* is another job's COMPUTED state; the ingress declares one job per role with no upstream needs, and computed output is logic that belongs in the reusable.

column1: hashfiles
column4: hashFiles(...) reads the checked-out repo tree — a filesystem/repo-state read the Actions service cannot do pre-runner and that a thin caller (no steps/run) has no place to perform.

column1: repo-identity
column4: github.repository is repo IDENTITY, not an event predicate; gating a role on which repo it is is enrollment/config, expressed by adopting the ingress, not by an if:.

column1: default-branch
column4: default_branch is repo CONFIGURATION that merely rides in the payload; it is a snapshot of repo state, not the triggering delta. Use github.event.pull_request.base.ref for the branch the event is actually about.

column1: labels-array-contains
column4: The pull_request.labels array is a human-mutated repo-state SNAPSHOT carried in the payload, not the triggering change; scanning it makes the if: gate on standing repo state. Use github.event.label.name (the labeled delta) instead.

column1: event-name
column4: github.event_name IS the event that woke the ingress — the canonical pure event predicate.

column1: event-action
column4: github.event.action is the event's own action field — a pure predicate over the delivered event, no repo-state reach.

column1: label-name
column4: github.event.label.name is the SINGLE label whose add/remove triggered the event — the triggering delta itself, contrast the standing labels array.

column1: base-ref
column4: base.ref is a plain payload field describing the PR that triggered the event; reading it as a predicate is an event filter, contrast repository.default_branch.
